Design system · one content model, many surfaces

The preview contract

OpenGraph-shaped previews · every document · every surface

Every surface in Barkpark today hand-builds its own document summary — Studio rows, desk tree, taskboard cards, the web finder, the TUI — and the public paper reader ships zero share metadata. This paper adopts the Open Graph protocol's real idea as our internal contract: any object becomes a rich card from four required properties plus typed extensions — computed once at write time, rendered identically everywhere, and emitted outward as og:/twitter:/JSON-LD for the web to unfurl.

North star
ONE preview manifest per document, derived at write time like content["body"] — never hand-built per surface. Any consumer renders a valid card from the core alone (graceful degradation is a testable invariant). Outward share metadata is EMITTED from the manifest, never separately authored.

1 · Where we stand

SurfaceToday
Papers reader /papers/:slugStatic <title>Paper · Barkpark</title>, ZERO og tags — a shared link unfurls as nothing. The single biggest gap.
Sheets readerTwo hand-authored tags (og:title + canned description); no image.
Studio doc rowstitle/status + schema-declared list_preview badge/meta (text only, per-type hand mapping, mirrored into the Go SDK).
Desk structure treeNav skeleton only — nodes carry {id, title, icon, type, filter}; no counts, no previews. Serves Studio AND the TUI desk from one contract (keep that).
web finderHand-builds og in generateMetadata with a per-type description switch; no og:image although the SDK imageUrl() helper exists.
Taskboard / projects / ticketsEach hand-selects {doc_id, title, content} and derives its own summary.

Everything the contract needs already exists server-side: titles are already projected to content["title"], the role:"featured" block doctrine marks the lead image, media renditions carry width/height variants, and client.imageUrl() exists in the JS SDK. The only genuinely new code is the featured-image extraction and one pure projection function.

2 · The contract — three rings, stolen from ogp.me

Ring 1, the required core (every doc type, no exceptions): title · type · image · url — plus description as the first optional. The core alone must render a usable card on every surface: desk row, Studio pane, share unfurl, TUI line.

Ring 2, the discriminator: preview.type selects the extension namespace, exactly as og:type selects article:*/book:*. Ours maps from the doc type: paper/post → article, everything else → website outwardly; internally the discriminator is the doc type itself.

Ring 3, namespaced extensions — never a god-object: paper carries published_time · authors[] · tags[] · section; task carries status · assignee · done_ratio; sheet carries tab_count; ticket carries key · state. A new doc type adds one extension schema and touches neither the core nor any existing consumer.

The image is a typed sub-object: image: { url, width, height, alt, type } — dimensions let surfaces reserve layout with no reflow; alt is the text bridge the TUI and email renderers need where pixels can't go.

Fallback resolvers, first-non-empty wins (ordered, debuggable, no magic): image = featured block → first body image → type default → site default; description = explicit excerpt → first body paragraph → empty; title = bound title → role:"title" block → row title.

3 · Where it computes — a derived index, not a query-time favor

A pure Barkpark.Preview.project/1 folded into the project-on-write walk beside Projection.project/3 — the preview persists like content["body"], computed once, read everywhere, cannot drift. Served as a preview key on the query envelope (NOT via /v1/preview — that name is the draft-perspective tunnel, a different concern). Envelope.render is not the seam — it is leaky by prior audit; the write-time projection is the safe one.

The one new extraction
og:image = walk free blocks for role:"featured" with a non-empty src (else first image block), resolved through Media.Delivery renditions. Add a dedicated og rendition preset at 1200×630 (1.91:1) beside thumb/preview/hero — the one size that unfurls correctly on every platform in 2026.

4 · Outward emission — the unified-aesthetic pattern again

The manifest EMITS the web layers; nobody hand-authors them: (1) the full og:* block — the universal substrate Slack, Discord, iMessage, WhatsApp, Telegram, LinkedIn and AI-chat unfurlers all read; (2) twitter:card = summary_large_image plus nothing else (X falls back to og; note og uses property=, twitter uses name=); (3) JSON-LD Article/Organization/Breadcrumb on public content only — that layer feeds search and AI answer engines, not unfurls; (4) oEmbed only for genuinely embeddable types — Slack PREFERS oEmbed over og when both exist, so shipping it carelessly downgrades static cards. Meta tags land early in <head>: Slack reads only the first 32 KB.

og:image size1200 × 630 (1.91:1); safe zone center ~1080 × 600; target < 300 KB; always emit width/height
og:title~60 chars before truncation
og:description1–2 sentences; ~110 chars safe, 155–200 max
Canonical og:urlexactly one per document — identity AND dedup key

5 · Consumers that collapse onto it

1. Papers + Sheets readers — emit the og/twitter/JSON-LD head from the manifest (papers go from zero to full share cards).
2. web finder — generateMetadata reads preview; deletes its per-type description switch; gains og:image via imageUrl().
3. Studio rows + Go TUI — list_preview badge/meta subsumed by the manifest's typed extensions; one PreviewSpec contract both sides.
4. Taskboard / projects / tickets cards — swap hand-built selects for the projection.
5. Desk structure — tree nodes stay a nav skeleton but may carry counts and a lead-doc thumbnail from the same manifest (coordinated with the studio-structure-polish epic's tiered desk).

6 · The waves

Open the same doc in Studio, the desk, the web finder and the TUI and see THE SAME card fields — because there is only one place they are computed. A core-only preview renders a valid card on every surface (the degradation test).
